The sky is blue due to a phenomenon called **Rayleigh scattering**. 

Sunlight may appear white, but it's made up of all the colors of the rainbow. As this light reaches Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules (primarily nitrogen and oxygen). These molecules scatter shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) much more than longer wavelengths (red, yellow, orange).

But why blue and not violet? Our eyes are more sensitive to blue light,
